thread:
Elaine Park (Sales): FYI large finance prospect (Catalyst) requested a POC with their 35B custom variant. They care about latency (<=250ms p95), prefix caching, and KMS/HSM for keying. Also asked for token pricing estimate.
Alex Chen: thanks — is that the quantized variant or full-fp32 they want to test?
Elaine Park (Sales): they mentioned 'catalyst-35b-custom-v1-qat' in their infra doc. attached a short spec (link).
Maria Gomez: @Alex can we run a quick compatibility sweep for that variant? KV cache + QAT path are the main asks. If not ready, what fallback model would keep SLOs?
Alex Chen: we can run an asap bench but need the model files and tokenizer. QAT may be fine; main questions: layer norm flavor (rmsnorm vs rmsnorm-fused) and attention kernel shape. If tokenizer differs we'll need a small adapter.
Elaine Park (Sales): I'll ping them for model tarball and tokenizer. timeline: they want POC demo next Wed (7 days).
Devon Patel: for Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoff: Dedicated will guarantee the latency under our SLA if they commit, hosted might hit cold-starts for a large kv-cache. Also need to know GPU memory footprint — 35B QAT could be ~40-60GB depending on kernels.
Samir Kapoor: security note: they require HSM-backed KMS and an SOC2 + PenTest report. Also a short questionnaire asking about access controls and model artifact provenance. Elaine — please send questionnaire now, we can loop legal.
Elaine Park (Sales): will do, sending now. Quick pricing Q: they want an estimate for 3-month POC at ~10 qps steady, bursts to 50. Any ballpark?
Devon Patel: rough hosted estimate: at 10 qps with batching and QAT, ~0.06–0.12 $/token depending on token lengths. For Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly) we should quote a commit that covers 10 qps and burst buffer; ping salesops for exact numbers.
Maria Gomez: action items: 1) Alex to run variant compatibility sweep on a small parsing dataset; 2) Devon to check memory + latency numbers on a 350-token median scenario; 3) Samir to review sec questionnaire; 4) Elaine to get model + tokenizer + business answers.
Alex Chen: I'll start a local run — sample command (local shim):
```
curl -X POST https://local-redwood.dev/infer
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST"
  -d '{"model":"catalyst-35b-custom-v1-qat","input":"<demo prompt>","kv_cache":true,"max_tokens":300}'
```
I'll post perf numbers here within 24h.
Devon Patel: note: if we see kv cache IO pressure we can suggest kv prewarm policy and prefix caching. That usually recovers p95 nicely.
Samir Kapoor: legal/infosec asks: can we bind the HSM attestation logs to their tenant? If private deployment yes, if hosted we need to confirm with infra. I'll start the questionnaire draft.
Elaine Park (Sales): thanks team. Catalyst also asked about fallback rules: they want automatic fallback to a smaller 16B variant on overload but preserve tokenization parity. Can we support auto-routing?
Alex Chen: yes — we can route to catalog variant 'catalyst-16b-compat' and keep tokenizer adapter. Need to validate output quality with their eval set.
Maria Gomez: I'll schedule a short eval run (100 prompts) comparing 35B vs 16B for client-critical intents. Results posted in this thread.
InfraBot: queued benchmark job #bnk-9123 for model catalyst-35b-custom-v1-qat. Estimated completion: 22 hours.
Elaine Park (Sales): awesome — will update Catalyst that we have a benchmark in progress and legal is reviewing sec q. Closing loop: can we aim for a preliminary perf + cost estimate by tomorrow EOD?
Alex Chen: yes — I'll post numbers and a short summary.
Devon Patel: I'll add memory/instance sizing + a suggested Dedicated commit.
Samir Kapoor: I'll share the questionnaire draft for review before sending.
Elaine Park (Sales): perfect. :thumbsup:
